sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Ruby concurrency interviews divide into two layers: the MRI GVL (Global VM Lock, often called GIL) which is the foundational constraint, and the concurrency primitives built on top of it — Thread, Mutex, Fiber, and the newer Ractor introduced in Ruby 3. The GVL means MRI threads cannot execute Ruby code in true parallel, but they do release the lock during IO — which is why Puma can serve multiple requests concurrently with threads even under MRI. This page covers Thread lifecycle and safety, Mutex.synchronize, the cooperative Fiber model, Ractor's share-nothing approach to true parallelism, the async gem for event-driven IO over Fibers, and the practical question engineers actually face: when to use Puma threads vs Unicorn processes for your Rails app workload.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: threads-mutex, fibers-ractor, gvl-internals, async-gem. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
